Václav Havel Bursary is a Charles University-wide hardship bursary for international students already admitted and enrolled in any degree programme at any CU faculty. No supervising professor or specific programme is attached to the bursary by design. Administration: applications go to the faculty Student Affairs Office; the Václav Havel Bursary Board (chair: prof. MUDr. Michal Vrablík, Vice-Rector for International Affairs; members: prof. PhDr. Lenka Rovná, Mgr. Alena Vlasáková, doc. JUDr. Jakub Tomšej) is an administrative body, not an academic supervision body; administrative contact: Kamila Verfelová, International Relations Office, kamila.verfelova@ruk.cuni.cz. Official source: https://cuni.cz/UKEN-2329.html

International Visegrad Fund regional mobility scholarship usable at more than 190 accredited higher-education institutions across Central and Eastern Europe for 1-2 semesters. Host institution, acceptance letter and research plan/supervision are arranged individually by the applicant; no institution or professor is attached to the scholarship itself. Official source: https://www.visegradfund.org/visegrad-scholarship-program-apply

CTU Scholarship for Foreign Students is a university-wide scholarship at Czech Technical University in Prague covering Master's and doctoral study across all CTU faculties. The official scholarship rules (https://international.cvut.cz/students/incoming-students/ctu-scholarships) name no supervisors; applications are submitted via the faculty International Office and decided by the vice-rector on the recommendation of a commission of vice-deans for international relations. For the doctoral strand, CTU states that candidates must specify an intended supervisor chosen from the selection presented on the faculty's website (https://international.cvut.cz/students/incoming-students/phd-programme-in-english/), so no individual supervisor can be tied to this scholarship without inventing a link.

Danish Government Scholarship at the University of Copenhagen is a Danish government-funded scheme granting full/partial tuition fee waivers and/or living-expense grants. All non-EU/EEA applicants offered admission to a Master's programme are considered automatically during admission assessment; there is no application and no supervising professor or specific programme tied to the award (faculty-specific limits apply, e.g. Faculty of Theology, Social Sciences). Official source: https://www.ku.dk/studies/masters/application-and-admission/scholarships
